text:
tara: Quick sync — follow-up on the Dedicated pool orchestration RFC. After pairing with infra we think the pragmatic path is: (1) split admit from allocate (client gets a short-lived admission token), (2) keep a backward-compatible header for v1 calls, and (3) ship an operator shim for at least 14 days. Need signoffs on token shape, TTL, and canary plan.
ashok: Thumbs up on split. What's the proposed token shape? need to ensure it's both opaque and verifiable without extra DB hits.
tara: Proposal: opaque string that encodes: version|expiry|nonce|sig (base64url). Sig = HMAC over (version|expiry|nonce) using operator key. Advantages: stateless validation, short TTL, easy rotation.
brynn: HMAC key rotation: operator should support key IDs in token and accept previous keys for a grace window. Add a metrics counter for token.sig_mismatch and token.expired.
ciara: TTL? Short TTL reduces replay but causes more exec calls. I suggest 30s-2m default, configurable per-tenant. Also allow a "hold-for-alloc" flag when callers want the old behavior (blocking).
tara: Good point. We'll default 60s. Add an optional admit param block_until_allocated=true for compatibility clients; operator will honor it if running in compatibility/shim mode.
ashok: How do we handle RBAC/ephemeral creds? If exec needs to perform privileged attach ops we should avoid encoding credentials in the token. Token should be a pointer; operator will map it server-side to ephemeral credentials minted with limited scope and TTL.
brynn: For observability: span names operator.admit.v3 and operator.allocate.v3 (not exec to vary wording). Add tags: feature_flag, tenant_id, admit_size, hold_flag. Record histogram for admit->allocate latency.
ciara: CI/contract tests: add a matrix: v1 single-call success, v1 single-call error paths, v2 admit-only -> allocate-ok, v2 admit-only -> allocate-timeout, and v2 block_until_allocated true. Include flaky-resilience test where node provisioning is delayed.
tara: Example smoke:
```bash
# v2 admit -> allocate flow
curl -X POST $OP/admit -H "X-API-Version: v2" -d '{"tenant":"team-a","slots":4}' | jq -r .token > t.txt
# token looks like: v3|1650619200|r4nd0m|b64sig
curl -X POST $OP/allocate -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat t.txt)"
```
ashok: Rollout plan draft: 1) ship operator with shim that accepts v1 and v2 tokens (long-lived) to staging; 2) enable control-plane v2 header for 5% of tenants in staging; 3) run contract suite and perf harness; 4) deploy to prod with operator shim enabled cluster-wide but control-plane flag off; 5) flip control-plane to v2 for 10% tenants (canary) for 72h; 6) if metrics good, expand to 50% and monitor for 7d; 7) after 14 days of stable metrics, remove shim by enabling strict-mode on canary operator then full roll.
brynn: Define rollback gates: token.sig_mismatch spike > 0.5% for 1h, admit->allocate latency regression > 30% P95, or error-rate increase > 0.2% absolute. If triggered, revert control-plane flag and scale operator back to shim image.
ciara: SDK changes: add OrchClient.admit(..., block_until_allocated=false) and OrchClient.allocate(token). Encourage SDKs to batch allocate for bursty workloads and add exponential backoff jitter for allocate polls. Debounce recommendations should be in devex notes.
tara: Telemetry: emit operator.api.v2_admit, operator.api.v2_allocate_success, operator.api.v2_allocate_timeout, operator.token.kms_reencrypt_count. Also add a debug endpoint /token/inspect (auth-only) to help support.
ashok: Security: ensure token signature uses rotating key stored in KMS; operator must support verifying both new and previous keys during rotation window. Add an alert for key-rotation-failures.
brynn: Ops: add a k8s readiness check that verifies operator can validate tokens with current keys. Rollout scripts should fail fast if readiness fails for > 2 min.
ciara: Backcompat lint: add a CI grep that looks for patterns where code calls admit and immediately assumes allocation (admit(); wait_for_node();). Flag those with a big comment to migrate to allocate() path.
tara: Docs/runbook: include sample curl, SDK snippets, canary checklist, rollback steps, and perf impact numbers (we saw 15% lower median latency for admit when non-blocking but 8% increase in allocate RPCs).

brynn: small nit: prefer "allocate" over "exec" in naming to avoid confusion with runtime exec.
tara: noted. We'll normalize to admit/allocate everywhere in the docs.
ciara: LGTM. I'll open tickets for tracing spans, metrics, and the CI lint.
tara: Thanks — I'll post the runbook and a PR for the operator shim. tagging @deploy-bot to create reminders for canary cadence.
deploy-bot: Reminder created: run v2 canary checklist in 3 days (staging) and 9 days (prod canary). :spiral_calendar:
